title: Topological superconductivity in layered d-wave altermagnetic metals
abstract: We investigate multilayer d-wave altermagnetic metals with odd-parity helical p-wave pairing. In the minimal bilayer system, interlayer tunneling reconstructs the spin-split Fermi surfaces and generates two layer-hybridized sectors with distinct effective chemical potentials. Without Rashba spin-orbit coupling (RSOC), the emergent mirror symmetry and subsystem chiral symmetry stabilize phases with different numbers of helical Majorana edge-mode pairs and additional counterpropagating pairs, jointly characterized by the mirror Chern number and the winding numbers defined along high-symmetry lines. The combination of RSOC and the altermagnetic exchange field gaps out the helical Majorana pairs while, in a certain parameter regime, leaving another pair of counterpropagating Majorana edge modes gapless, giving rise to second-order topological phases with isolated or twofold Majorana corner modes, as well as a hybrid-order phase in which gapless Majorana edge modes coexist with Majorana corner modes. We identify a layer symmetry that elucidates the physical origin of these phases. For an arbitrary N-layer system, such a symmetry naturally arises from the interlayer-coupling matrix, allowing N-fold Majorana corner modes to emerge when all layer-hybridized sectors enter the nontrivial second-order regime. Our results establish the interplay among the layer degree of freedom, odd-parity pairing, and Fermi-surface configurations as a controllable route to engineering topological superconductivity in layered altermagnetic systems.
summary: This work theoretically explores how topological superconductivity can be engineered in layered altermagnetic metals by controlling the interplay between layer structure, odd-parity pairing, and spin-orbit coupling. The authors demonstrate that these systems host tunable higher-order topological phases, characterized by specific Majorana edge and corner modes. This provides a robust theoretical framework for designing novel superconducting quantum materials.
main_problem: The paper investigates the emergence and control of topological superconductivity in layered d-wave altermagnetic metals.
main_result: The combination of layer degrees of freedom, odd-parity pairing, and Fermi-surface geometry allows for the engineering of tunable topological phases, including second-order and hybrid-order superconducting states.
method: The analysis uses symmetry protection (mirror and chiral symmetry) applied to the Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) Hamiltonian to characterize topological invariants.
model_or_system: The model is a multilayer d-wave altermagnetic metal with odd-parity helical p-wave pairing, analyzed via the BdG Hamiltonian for a minimal bilayer system, which is later generalized to N layers.
key_observables: Mirror Chern number, winding numbers, gapless Majorana edge modes, and Majorana corner modes.
important_parameters: Interlayer tunneling ($\eta$), Rashba spin-orbit coupling ($\lambda_{so}$), and the chemical potential ($\mu$).
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses on the spin-triplet pairing component and neglects even-parity spin-singlet components.
figures_summary: The figures illustrate the evolution of Fermi-surface configurations under varying chemical potentials, linking specific topological invariants ($C_M$) to the predicted number and type of Majorana edge states.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from analyzing the minimal bilayer model and its first-order topological phases, to detailing the emergence of second- and hybrid-order phases, and finally generalizing the findings to an arbitrary N-layer system based on a layer symmetry.
why_interesting: The explicit connection between magnetic order (altermagnetism), pairing symmetry (odd-parity), and topological superconductivity provides a concrete, material-based platform for realizing exotic superconducting states relevant to quantum materials research.

The parameters are t = 1, η = 0.8, λso = 0, and tAM = 0.2.

Lower panels: Energy spectra of the corresponding superconducting phases under open (periodic) boundary conditions in the x (y) direction, with pairing amplitude ∆p = 0.3. The red, blue, cyan and green solid lines represent nondegenerate, doubly degenerate, triple degenerate and quadruple degenerate edge states, respectively. (a) µ = −4, (b) µ = −2, (c) µ = −1, (d) µ = 1, (e) µ = 2, and (f) µ = 4. Common parameters are t = 1, η = 0.8, λso = 0, and tAM = 0.2.
FIG. 3. Topological phase diagram as a function of µ. Parameters are chosen as t = 1, η = 0.8, λso = 0, ∆p = 0.3 and tAM = 0.2.
